authoring.value:
Let $D$ be a finite region enclosed by the curve $\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}=1.$ If 

$$
f(x,y)={\begin{aligned}x\operatorname{sin}⁡y, & (x,y)\in R\cap D \\ 0, & (x,y)\in R∖D\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,{∬}_{D}x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

Require $D\subseteq R$, so the rectangle contains the entire region. Which of the following could be the definition of the rectangular domain $R?$

- $R=[-2,2]\times [-3,3]$
- $R=[-2,2]\times [-2,2]$
- $R=[-2,2]\times [-3,1]$

authoring.value:
The ellipse $x^2/4+y^2/9\le1$ has horizontal extent $[-2,2]$ and vertical extent $[-3,3]$. Rectangle I contains the entire ellipse. Rectangles II and III both exclude the ellipse's point $(0,3)$. Thus only I satisfies the stated containment requirement.

For a containing rectangle, $f=x\sin y$ on $D$ and $f=0$ on $R\setminus D$, so $\iint_R f\,dA=\iint_D x\sin y\,dA$. The correct study answer is "I only".

The original unqualified equality alone admits all three rectangles: $D$ and each $R\cap D$ are symmetric under $x\mapsto-x$, while $x\sin y$ changes sign. Every such integral is zero. The explicit requirement $D\subseteq R$ removes this accidental-cancellation ambiguity.
